marks.gloss_en: אין, דתניא: רבי מונא אמר משום רבי יהודה פת הבאה בכסנין מברכין עליה המוציא (kind svara: no SupportKind names דתניא)
ואמר שמואל הלכה כרבי מונא -- Shmuel's ruling as the company cite it
the company were saying 'who brings forth bread from the earth' over pat haba bekisanin
שאני יין דגורם ברכה לעצמו -- wine is different, for it occasions a blessing by itself
עדי כפנא! אלא כל שאחרים קובעים עליו סעודה צריך לברך -- that is [a meal that] satisfies hunger; whatever others fix a meal on requires a blessing (unanswered)
Rav Huna ate thirteen loaves, three to a kav, and did not bless
אין הלכה כרבי מונא איתמר -- the ruling you rely on was stated the other way (the company reply by attacking his tradition, not by answering)
והא מר הוא דאמר משמיה דשמואל: לחמניות מערבין בהן ומברכין עליהן המוציא -- you yourself report Shmuel saying hamotzi over wafers
שאני התם דקבע סעודתיה עלייהו, אבל היכא דלא קבע סעודתיה עלייהו -- לא: there he fixed his meal on them; where he does not, no hamotzi
Shmuel (as Rav Yehuda reports him): the halakha is NOT like R' Mona -- that is what was stated
לא סבר לה מר גמר אסור מלאכול? -- does the master not hold that once one has finished, one may not eat?
סלק איתמר -- the dictum reads 'removed', not 'finished'
after they finished their meal, something to eat was brought; Rav Pappa took it and ate
לא סבר לה מר סלק אסור מלאכול? -- does the master not hold that once [the table] is removed, one may not eat?
אנן אתכא דריש גלותא סמכינן -- we rely on the Exilarch's table [which has not been removed]
after the table was removed, a portion was sent from the Exilarch's house; Rava ate
one who blessed over the wine before the meal has exempted the wine after the meal
if they were sitting, each one blesses for himself
אלא כי הא דאמר רבי חייא בר אשי אמר רב: שלש תכיפות הן... תכף לנטילת ידים ברכה
Rav: one accustomed to oil -- the oil holds him back
Abaye: we too will say -- immediately upon Torah scholars, blessing
